title: A power series: radius, interval, a derivative and a geometric sum

stimulus.title: The power series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>
stimulus.html:
The function ff is defined by the power series f(x)f(x)=∑n=1∞(x−2)nn⋅5n= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 5^n} for all xx where the series converges. Its first three terms are shown.
The first three terms of ∑n=1∞(x−2)nn⋅5n\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 5^n}
nn112233
Termx−25\frac{x - 2}{5}(x−2)250\frac{(x - 2)^2}{50}(x−2)3375\frac{(x - 2)^3}{375}

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the radius of convergence of the series for ff.

rubric.point: Sets up the ratio with absolute values and finds its limit: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{n \to \infty} \left|\frac{(x - 2)^{n+1}}{(n + 1)5^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 5^n}{(x - 2)^n}\right|</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{|x - 2|}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: the limit written with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n \to \infty</annotation></semantics></math> and absolute value bars

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x - 2| < 5</annotation></semantics></math>, so the radius is 5

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right|</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{|x - 2|^{n+1}}{(n + 1)5^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 5^n}{|x - 2|^n}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{|x - 2|}{5} \cdot \frac{n}{n + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{n \to \infty} \left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right|</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{|x - 2|}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. The series converges when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{|x - 2|}{5} < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, that is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x - 2| < 5</annotation></semantics></math>. The radius of convergence is 5.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the interval of convergence of the series for ff. Justify your answer at each endpoint.

rubric.point: Right endpoint: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 7</annotation></semantics></math> the series is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{1}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, the harmonic series, which diverges

Left endpoint: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -3</annotation></semantics></math> the series is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, which converges by the alternating series test, with the conditions stated (alternates; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{n}</annotation></semantics></math> decreases and approaches 0)
accept: "alternating harmonic series, which converges" with the conditions of the alternating series test

rubric.point: Interval <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-3, 7)</annotation></semantics></math>, consistent with the endpoint conclusions

parts.sample: From part (a), the series converges for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3 < x < 7</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 7</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{5^n}{n \cdot 5^n} = \sum \frac{1}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, the harmonic series, which diverges. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{(-5)^n}{n \cdot 5^n}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>; the terms alternate in sign, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{n}</annotation></semantics></math> decreases and approaches 0, so this series converges by the alternating series test. The interval of convergence is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-3, 7)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the value of f‴(2)f'''(2).

rubric.point: Identifies the coefficient of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 2)^3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>375</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3 \cdot 5^3} = \frac{1}{375}</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f'''(2)}{3!}</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The series is the Taylor series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so the coefficient of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 2)^3</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f'''(2)}{3!}</annotation></semantics></math>. That coefficient is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>125</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>375</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3 \cdot 125} = \frac{1}{375}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'''(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>375</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3! \cdot \frac{1}{375}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>375</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{6}{375}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>125</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2}{125}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write the power series for f′(x)f'(x), using sigma notation. Then use it to find the exact value of ∑n=1∞2n−15n\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2^{n-1}}{5^n}.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^{n-1}}{5^n}</annotation></semantics></math>, from term-by-term differentiation
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>25</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \frac{x - 2}{25}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>125</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \frac{(x - 2)^2}{125}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo>⋯</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \cdots</annotation></semantics></math> with the general term

rubric.point: Recognizes the sum as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>, a geometric series with first term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> and ratio <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>, and finds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1/5}{1 - 2/5} = \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Differentiating term by term, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 5^n}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{n(x - 2)^{n-1}}{n \cdot 5^n}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^{n-1}}{5^n}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x - 2| < 5</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> this is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mfrac><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2^{n-1}}{5^n}</annotation></semantics></math>, a geometric series with first term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> and ratio <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. Its sum is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1/5}{1 - 2/5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1/5}{3/5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
